cues.zh: 嗨，我叫Tony，这里是《每一帧都是画》。
cues.en: Hi my name is Tony and this is Every Frame a Painting.

cues.zh: 今天我要聊一位我很喜欢的导演的作品。
cues.en: So today I’m going to talk about a director whose work I love.

cues.zh: 但在此之前，我先坦白说。我觉得今天的喜剧电影
cues.en: but before that let me be upfront. I think comedy movies today

cues.zh: 尤其是美国的，已经完全迷失了方向。
cues.en: especially American ones have totally lost their way.

cues.zh: 我不是讨厌那些笑话、演员或对白
cues.en: I don't hate the jokes or the actors or the dialogue

cues.zh: 也不是讨厌故事，虽然那里问题也不少。
cues.en: or the stories though there's plenty of issues there.

cues.zh: 我真正的不满在于，电影制作本身
cues.en: My real qualm is that the filmmaking

cues.zh: 用画面和声音来传递笑点的方式，简直……
cues.en: the use of picture and sound to deliver jokes, is just...

cues.zh: <i>--什么？ --这太无聊了。
cues.en: <i>--What? --This is booooring.
<i>--Delete.

cues.zh: 听着，每个人的品味都不同。
cues.en: Look, everyone’s taste is different.

cues.zh: 你觉得好笑就是好笑。所以我不是说这些电影很烂
cues.en: What you find funny is what you funny. So I’m not saying these movies suck

cues.zh: 也不是说喜欢它们的你很烂。我想说的是
cues.en: or you suck if you like them. What I am saying is that

cues.zh: 这些电影根本不算电影。它们只是轻度剪辑过的即兴表演。
cues.en: these movies aren’t movies. They’re lightly edited improv.

cues.zh: 每个人都站着不动，在特写镜头里互相说话。
cues.en: Everyone stands still and talks at each other in close-up.

cues.zh: 这些笑点几乎没有视觉上的，它们全是声音。
cues.en: Almost none of these jokes come visually They’re overwhelming sound.

cues.zh: 甚至不是完整的声音范围，只是对白。这真的很可悲
cues.en: And not even the full range of sound, just dialogue. And this is really sad

cues.zh: 因为这仅仅是电影所能做到的一小部分。
cues.en: because that’s just a fraction of what’s possible in cinema.

cues.zh: 除了动画和一些广告，
cues.en: Apart from animation and some commercials,

cues.zh: 视觉喜剧实际上在倒退。这就是为什么
cues.en: visual comedy is actually moving backwards. And that's why

cues.zh: 如果你喜欢这类东西，我怎么推荐Edgar Wright都不为过。
cues.en: if you love this kind of stuff, I cannot recommend Edgar Wright enough.

cues.zh: <i>--你是医生，处理一下。--是啊，混蛋。
cues.en: <i>--You're a doctor, deal with it. --Yeah, motherfucker.

cues.zh: 他是这个类型中仅有的几个充分利用一切可能性的人之一
cues.en: He's one of the only people working in the genre using the full range of what is possible

cues.zh: 正因为如此，他能在别人不看的地方找到幽默。
cues.en: And because of that, he can find humor in places that others don’t look.

cues.zh: 举个例子。假设你需要把你的角色
cues.en: Here’s an example. Say you need to move your character

cues.zh: 从一个城市移到另一个城市来推动故事。你怎么拍？
cues.en: from one city to another to get the story going. How do you shoot it?

cues.zh: 能从中挖出个笑话吗？……好吧，不能。
cues.en: And can you get a joke out of it? ...Well, no.

cues.zh: 但如果你派第二摄制组去拍，每个镜头都从左往右摇
cues.en: Not if you send out a 2nd unit to do it, every shot pans from left to right

cues.zh: 你加上显眼的地标和标志，再混入通用的直升机航拍素材
cues.en: you include obvious landmarks and signs, you mix in generic helicopter footage

cues.zh: 然后在下面配上欢快的音乐，让观众不至于无聊。
cues.en: and you put upbeat music under it so the audience doesn’t get bored.

cues.zh: 这就是偷懒的拍法，还很无聊。这种我们见过一百万次了。
cues.en: This is just lazy filmmaking and boring. We’ve seen it a million times.

cues.zh: 如果这类场景你真能拍得别出心裁，会怎样？
cues.en: What would happen if you were truly inventive with this type of scene?

cues.zh: 这就对了！而且这不只是一连串快速剪辑。
cues.en: There we go! And this isn’t just a series of quick cuts.

cues.zh: 这里有大量出色的视觉叙事。
cues.en: There’s a lot of good visual storytelling here.

cues.zh: 这两个出租车镜头清楚地告诉你我们从哪来、要到哪去
cues.en: These two taxi shots tell you exactly where we came from and where we’re going

cues.zh: 这两个镜头强调了对文明的远离。
cues.en: These two shots emphasize the move away from civilization.

cues.zh: 我们的主角始终面朝前方或右侧
cues.en: Our main character always faces forward or to the right

cues.zh: 这样屏幕方向就保持一致。把音乐调小
cues.en: so screen direction is respected. Turning the music down

cues.zh: 把音效调大就很好笑，因为每个剪辑都很突兀。
cues.en: and the sound FX up is funny because each cut is jarring.

cues.zh: 连 Simon Pegg 和 Ryan Gosling 都有不错的表现。
cues.en: And there’s even some nice performances from Simon Pegg and Ryan Gosling.

cues.zh: 好，那是个没有上下文的例子。你说得对。完全不公平。
cues.en: Okay that was 1 example without context. You’re right. Totally unfair.

cues.zh: 那如果有一部电影，里面发生了可怕的末日事件，
cues.en: Well what if you had a movie where a horrible apocalyptic event happens,

cues.zh: 你想提前埋下伏笔，也许让角色
cues.en: and you want to foreshadow it earlier, maybe by having the characters

cues.zh: 没注意到电视上的重要信息。你会怎么表现？
cues.en: not notice something important on TV. How would you show it?

cues.zh: 你会直接把它塞进剪辑里，只给两秒两帧
cues.en: Would you just throw it in the edit for 2 seconds and 2 frames

cues.zh: 而且没有任何镜头展现角色和电视之间的关系吗？
cues.en: and no shot shows the relationship between the characters and the TV?

cues.en: Okay still unfair. What if you had movie where one character has stopped drinking

cues.en: but the others are disappointed in him and you want to get a joke out of it.

cues.zh: 你会怎么做？
cues.en: How would you do it?

cues.en: Would they just stand around and talk about his drinking?

cues.en: <i>--No I appreciate it but I told my wife I wouldn't drink tonight

cues.en: <i>--Besides I got a big day tomorrow. You guys have a great time.

cues.en: --Big day? Doing what? Or would you do this? --What?!

cues.en: <i>--I don't believe this.

cues.zh: 这就是平庸导演和伟大导演的区别。能力
cues.en: This is what separates a mediocre director from a great one. The ability

cues.zh: 在于把最平淡无奇的场景找出新的拍法。
cues.en: to take the most simple mundane scenes and find new ways to do them.

cues.zh: 伟大的导演明白，仅靠场面调度就能制造笑点。
cues.en: Great directors understand that you can get a laugh just through staging.

cues.zh: David Bordwell举了个例子：东西突然闯入画面很好笑。
cues.en: Here’s an example from David Bordwell: things popping up into frame are funny.

cues.zh: <i>--慢速前进，我可以慢速前进。下来撒点这玩意儿！
cues.en: <i>--Slow ahead, I can go slow ahead. Come on down and chum some of this shit!

cues.zh: 不只是东西进入画面。想想相反的情况。
cues.en: And it’s not just things entering frame. Consider the opposite.

cues.en: You can get a laugh from a zoom.

cues.en: <i>--You wanna pop the trunk and roll the windows down, please?

cues.en: You can get a laugh from a crane up. <i>--Shirley, I'm so sorry.

cues.en: You can get a laugh from a pan.

cues.zh: 正如Martin Scorsese所说
cues.en: As Martin Scorsese put it

cues.zh: 电影的关键在于画面里有什么，以及画面里没有什么。
cues.en: cinema is a matter of what’s in the frame and what’s not in the frame.

cues.zh: 所以好好想想画面构图。这跟喜剧是高明还是低俗无关。
cues.en: So think about the frame. And this isn’t a matter of smart or stupid comedy.

cues.zh: 真的，只要有效果，就是好手法。
cues.en: Really if it works, it works.

cues.zh: 下面就是Edgar Wright用画面和声音做到的8件事
cues.en: So here are 8 things Edgar Wright does with picture and sound that

cues.zh: 我希望其他喜剧电影人也来试试。
cues.en: I want to see other comedy filmmakers try out.

cues.zh: #1 用搞笑的方式让东西进入画面
cues.en: #1 Things entering the frame in funny ways

cues.zh: #2 用搞笑的方式让人物离开画面
cues.en: #2 People leaving the frame in funny ways

cues.zh: #3 去了又回
cues.en: #3 There and back again

cues.zh: #4 匹配的场景转场
cues.en: #4 Matching scene transitions

cues.zh: #5 时机完美的音效
cues.en: #5 The perfectly-timed sound effect

cues.zh: #6 动作与音乐同步
cues.en: #6 Action synchronized to the music

cues.zh: #7 超级戏剧化的灯光变化
cues.en: #7 Super-dramatic lighting cues

cues.zh: #8 围栏笑料
cues.en: #8 Fence gags

cues.zh: 对了，再加上#9 想象中的枪战
cues.en: And you know what, let's thrown in #9 Imaginary gunfights

cues.zh: 所以如果你是电影人，就在这方面下功夫。画面构图是个游乐场，尽情玩吧。
cues.en: So if you’re a filmmaker, work on this. The frame is a playground. So play.

cues.zh: 下次你去剧院花15美元看喜剧
cues.en: And the next time you go to a theater and pay $15 to see a comedy
